body: Yes, its a mess, we are aware, we would appreciate if you could help contribute to improving it! Thanks.
@kradalby  I can give it a shot. If no one has started it

Yes sure, I think a lot of the code is similar, and can probably be more reused.

This effort would probably benefit from some planning, outline how it currently is and where we want it to go.

Documentation is wrong, too ([doc](https://headscale.net/stable/setup/install/container/#register-a-machine-normal-login)). Making it hard for new users.

>Generate a key using the command line:
>```
>docker exec -it headscale \
>   headscale preauthkeys create --user myfirstuser --reusable --expiration 24h
>```

```
Error: invalid argument "myfirstuser" for "-u, --user" flag: strconv.ParseUint: parsing "myfirstuser": invalid syntax
```

Why would a user (created by username) suddenly be represented by an integer? Which isn't even logged when creating the user. So it needs a dedicated lookup and you need to remember the id. Makes no sense to me.

Interestingly this works, which is shown by the register URL:
```
headscale nodes register --user USERNAME --key NV4RcnRP7vaONKmTB7V12345
```
@kradalby I will update my current branch for this bug since I was already working on it a while back but not it's outdated.

> Generate a key using the command line:
> ```
> docker exec -it headscale \
>   headscale preauthkeys create --user myfirstuser --reusable --expiration 24h
> ```

I want to make aware that this has worked in earlier versions of headscale (at least in 0.25.1 because that is what its NixOS test at that time used, see [this line](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/da2b89022cf3da1045c8cc9bb5c816de22fdd788/nixos/tests/headscale.nix#L81)).
And actually I would be interested to know why this was changed 🤔

Huh, I just came across this again, maybe I can try contributing. Can't be that hard.... uh oh, don't jinx it! Probably not easy, else it would have been done? I guess would have to ensure lookup of user id everywhere, which would need to do db lookups, perhaps add a cache if one does not exist... uh oh.... But the foundation must be there, because the `acl.json` uses fully qualified usernames, and some of the commands do as well, so will have to take a dive into the code and see.

Trying to get headscale up and running again and figure out `acl.json`, tagging, etc., I just thought to myself:

**Q: What would Linux users worldwide say** if Linus Tarvolds suddenly changed the kernel to no longer accept alphanumeric usernames and required every `chown`, `su`, `setuid`, etc. command to use the numeric id instead?

**A: They would riot.** There would be torches, pitchforks, and a thousand new angry GitHub issues per hour after all programs/scripts stopped working and systems no longer booted. Power would blackout worldwide. Linus would get an earful (if the internet and all infrastructure weren't totally broken), he would hide in a cave, and the change would be reverted faster than you can say "systemd."
@tgrushka, I'm currently working on this. If you have any ideas and suggestions, do not hesitate to reach out!!! I always appreciate the feedback/suggestions. Thank you
This issue is stale because it has been open for 90 days with no activity.
